label: NIST
description: National Institute of Standards and Technology — US federal agency that standardized the first PQC algorithms
notes: NIST's PQC Standardization Project (launched 2016) selected ML-KEM (FIPS 203), ML-DSA (FIPS 204), and SLH-DSA (FIPS 205) as the first post-quantum standards, published August 2024. FN-DSA (FIPS 206) is not yet published as of 2026 (Falcon selected; draft pending). NIST IR 8547 defines the transition timeline: deprecate 112-bit classical asymmetric by 2030, disallow by 2035. NIST also runs CMVP (module validation) and CAVP (algorithm validation) programs that enforce these standards globally.

label: ENISA
description: European Union Agency for Cybersecurity — EU's PQC guidance authority and EUCC scheme co-manager
notes: ENISA published the landmark 2022 Post-Quantum Cryptography report and subsequent PQC guidelines adopted across EU member states. Co-manages the EUCC certification scheme with ECCG. Provides technical support for NIS2 implementation and coordinates EU-wide PQC migration readiness. ENISA's guidelines are the primary reference for EU organizations planning PQC transitions.

label: ISO/IEC JTC 1/SC 27
description: ISO/IEC Joint Technical Committee 1, Subcommittee 27 — international body standardizing PQC algorithms for global adoption
notes: ISO/IEC JTC 1/SC 27 Working Group 2 standardizes cryptographic mechanisms for global use. Key PQC work items: ISO/IEC 14888-4 (ML-DSA/Dilithium digital signatures, under development), ISO/IEC 18033 series (encryption, ML-KEM alignment). ISO standards often harmonize with NIST outputs to enable global adoption outside US jurisdiction. Relevant for organizations requiring internationally recognized standards beyond NIST FIPS.

label: IETF
description: Internet Engineering Task Force — open standards body integrating PQC algorithms into internet protocols (TLS, SSH, CMS, S/MIME)
notes: IETF's PQUIP (Post-Quantum Use In Protocols) working group coordinates PQC integration across the internet protocol stack. 30+ active RFCs and drafts for PQC in 2025-2026 including: RFC 9881/9882 (ML-DSA in X.509/CMS), RFC 9794 (hybrid terminology), RFC 9814 (SLH-DSA in CMS), draft-ietf-tls-ecdhe-mlkem (TLS 1.3 hybrid), draft-ietf-lamps-pq-composite-kem (composite KEM). 6+ drafts in RFC Editor Queue as of early 2026.

label: FIPS 140-3
description: NIST cryptographic module validation program
notes: CMVP validation will require PQC algorithm support. FIPS 203/204/205 already published. The 2030 date reflects NIST IR 8547's timeline for deprecating 112-bit classical asymmetric algorithms. Important milestone: all FIPS 140-2 certificates move to the Historical list on September 21 2026 — after that date only FIPS 140-3 validated modules may be procured for new federal systems.

label: Common Criteria
description: International security evaluation framework
notes: New protection profiles for PQC are being developed. Certification timelines vary by scheme.

label: ANSSI
description: French national cybersecurity agency regulation
deadline: 2025-2030 (phased; ANSSI recommendation, not a legal mandate)
notes: ANSSI recommends hybrid PQC for new systems via its position paper (not a legal mandate). Phase 2 (not before 2025): hybrid for PQC assurance; Phase 3 (not before 2030): standalone PQC optional. ANSSI issued its first PQC security certifications Sept-Oct 2025 (Thales MultiApp 5.2 Premium PQC, Samsung S3SSE2A).

label: CNSA 2.0
description: NSA mandate for national security systems
notes: NSA mandate for U.S. national security systems. Phased deadlines by category: software/firmware signing prefer 2025 exclusively 2030; web/cloud prefer 2025 exclusively 2033; networking prefer 2026 exclusively 2030; OS prefer 2027 exclusively 2033; niche/legacy 2030-2033. Revised May 2025 algorithm document specifies ML-KEM-1024, ML-DSA-87, AES-256, SHA-384/512, LMS/XMSS. Executive Order 14306 (June 2025) ties CNSA 2.0 to federal procurement mandates via CISA product category list.

notes: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/482 establishes EUCC as the EU-wide ICT product security certification scheme, replacing fragmented national Common Criteria schemes. label: ANSSI
description: Agence nationale de la sécurité des systèmes d'information — France's national cybersecurity authority
notes: ANSSI is France's primary cybersecurity authority, publishing PQC guidance since 2022. Key publications include the 2022 PQC Position Paper and 2024 Follow-Up Paper recommending hybrid PQC for new systems. ANSSI coordinates with ENISA and BSI on European PQC harmonization.

notes: CRYPTREC is a joint committee of Japan's Ministry of Internal Affairs (MIC) and METI. Publishes the CRYPTREC Ciphers List (approved algorithms for e-Government systems). Active PQC evaluation programme aligned with NIST outcomes. Annual technical reports cover PQC migration readiness.

label: KISA / NIS

notes: KISA (under MSIT) leads Korean internet security and runs the KpqC competition for domestic PQC algorithms. NIS oversees KCMVP (Korean Cryptographic Module Validation Program). label: OSCCA / SCA
description: Office of State Commercial Cryptography Administration (国家密码管理局) — China's regulatory authority for commercial cryptography
notes: OSCCA (now operating as SCA — State Cryptography Administration) regulates all commercial cryptography in China. Administers the SM-series algorithms (SM2/SM3/SM4) as national standards. label: IEEE 1609.2 PQC Amendment (V2X)
description: IEEE vehicular communications security standard update for PQC
notes: IEEE 1609.2 amendment adds ML-KEM and ML-DSA PQC support for vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communications security. Directly affects automotive OEMs and connected vehicle infrastructure.

label: OASIS PKCS#11 Technical Committee
description: OASIS technical committee defining the PKCS#11 HSM programming interface standard
notes: OASIS defines the PKCS#11 standard — the programming interface that every hardware security module implements. PQC mechanisms in v3.2 (ML-KEM, ML-DSA, SLH-DSA) will drive the entire HSM industry PQC adoption.

label: 3GPP Security Working Group
description: 3GPP SA3 — global mobile network security standards working group studying PQC integration
notes: 3GPP SA3 defines global mobile network security standards for 5G and 6G. Actively studying PQC integration into core network protocols. Distinct from ETSI and GSMA. TR 33.841 (PQC Study) approved May 2025.

label: FS-ISAC PQC Migration Guidance
description: Financial Services Information Sharing and Analysis Center PQC migration advisory
notes: FS-ISAC (Sept 2025) warns financial sector has not defined resources for PQC migration. Joint Europol-FS-ISAC report (Jan 2026) provides Quantum Risk Score framework and migration complexity assessment for financial institutions.

label: ASC X9 Financial PKI & PQC Standards
description: Accredited Standards Committee X9 develops cryptographic standards for the financial services industry. X9 Financial PKI (launched June 2025, with DigiCert) provides PQC-enabled certificate infrastructure for banks, payment terminals, and financial enterprises. Key PQC standards: X9.146 (Quantum TLS for financial services), X9 TR-50 (Quantum Techniques in CMS), and the X9 PQC Financial Readiness Needs Assessment (2025).
notes: X9 Financial PKI supports ML-KEM and ML-DSA alongside legacy algorithms for backward compatibility. X9.146 Quantum TLS draft in beta testing (2025). X9 is the primary ANSI-accredited standards body for financial cryptography in the US.

label: PKI Consortium
description: Industry consortium coordinating PQC readiness for PKI operators and certificate authorities
notes: PKI Consortium (pkic.org) organizes annual PQC conferences and publishes PQC migration guidance for certificate authorities. Active since 2013; PQC focus accelerated since 2023. Members include DigiCert, Sectigo, Keyfactor, Entrust. Published hybrid certificate guidance and interoperability testing reports for ML-DSA and composite certificates.

label: Cloud Security Alliance
description: Cloud Security Alliance Quantum-Safe Working Group developing quantum security controls for cloud environments
notes: CSA Quantum-Safe Security Working Group publishes guidance on quantum-safe cloud security controls. CCM v4 includes cryptographic governance controls applicable to PQC migration. CSA also maintains the Cloud Controls Matrix used by cloud providers for compliance attestation. Referenced by CSA quantum-safe guidelines cited in threat profiles CLOUD-001 through CLOUD-004.

label: ITU-T SG17
description: ITU Telecommunication Standardization Sector Study Group 17 on security standards for global telecom PQC transition
notes: ITU-T Study Group 17 (Security) includes Question 14/17 studying PQC for telecommunications networks. Develops X-series security recommendations. Coordinates with 3GPP SA3 and ETSI QSC on telecom PQC standardization. Focus areas include 5G/6G security architecture with PQC integration and quantum-safe key management for network operators.

label: NIST SP 800-208
description: NIST recommendation for stateful hash-based signature schemes (LMS and XMSS)
notes: NIST SP 800-208 specifies the Leighton-Micali Signature (LMS) and eXtended Merkle Signature Scheme (XMSS) for firmware signing and other stateful signature applications. Referenced by CNSA 2.0 as an approved signature algorithm for national security systems. Critical for firmware signing and code signing where stateful signatures are acceptable. Requires careful state management to prevent one-time key reuse.

label: ISO/IEC 19790:2024
description: International standard for security requirements for cryptographic modules — equivalent of FIPS 140-3
notes: ISO/IEC 19790:2024 (3rd edition) defines security requirements for cryptographic modules. International equivalent of NIST FIPS 140-3. Used by JCMVP (Japan), KCMVP (South Korea), and as the basis for EUCC cryptographic module evaluation. PQC algorithm testing requirements are being updated as ISO/IEC JTC 1/SC 27 publishes PQC standards. Organizations outside US jurisdiction often require ISO/IEC 19790 rather than FIPS 140-3. | 2026-07-13: original website URL (iso.org/standard/85063.html) resolved to a DIFFERENT standard entirely (ISO/IEC 4396-7:2023, telecommunications) -- corrected to the real, current ISO/IEC 19790:2025 catalog page.

label: ETSI GS QKD Series
description: ETSI Group Specification series for Quantum Key Distribution covering protocols interfaces and network management
notes: ETSI ISG QKD has published 18 specifications covering QKD protocol interfaces (GS QKD 004), key delivery APIs (GS QKD 014), network interoperability (GS QKD 018), and management. QKD complements PQC for defense-in-depth in high-assurance environments. India DST/NQM roadmap recommends hybrid PQC plus QKD. BSI and ANSSI have published joint position papers on QKD vs PQC trade-offs.

label: ANSSI Security Certification
description: French national cybersecurity certification scheme — issued world first PQC product certifications in 2025
deadline: Ongoing (voluntary PQC security visa; first PQC certs Sept-Oct 2025)
notes: ANSSI security certification scheme issued the world's first PQC product certifications (Sept-Oct 2025): Thales Smartcard MultiApp 5.2 Premium PQC (EAL5+) and Samsung S3SSE2A. PQC qualification is voluntary, not a 2027 mandate.
library_refs: ANSSI PQC Position Paper;ANSSI PQC Follow-up Paper;ANSSI-PQC-FAQ-2025;ANSSI-PG-083-v3-2026

label: JCMVP
description: Japanese Cryptographic Module Validation Program — Japan equivalent of NIST CMVP for government procurement
notes: JCMVP (Japanese Cryptographic Module Validation Program) is run by IPA (Information-technology Promotion Agency Japan). Japan equivalent of NIST CMVP/FIPS 140-3 based on ISO/IEC 19790 and JIS X 19790. Mandatory for Japanese government cryptographic module procurement. PQC algorithm integration is expected after CRYPTREC completes its PQC evaluation and publishes updated cipher recommendations.

label: Singapore CSA Quantum-Safe Handbook
description: Singapore Cyber Security Agency national guidelines for quantum-safe transition across all sectors
notes: CSA Singapore published the National Quantum-Safe Handbook providing comprehensive PQC migration guidance for all sectors. Goes beyond MAS financial circular (MAS-CIRCULAR) to cover government, telecom, and technology sectors. Includes algorithm selection guidance aligned with NIST FIPS 203/204/205, migration planning templates, and industry-specific recommendations. Singapore also runs a QKD Sandbox program.

label: Brazil LGPD/ANPD PQC Guidance
description: Brazilian data protection authority ANPD guidance on cryptographic requirements under LGPD with PQC implications
notes: Brazil Lei Geral de Protecao de Dados (LGPD) requires appropriate technical measures including encryption for personal data protection. ANPD (Autoridade Nacional de Protecao de Dados) has published guidance on security measures. While no explicit PQC mandate exists, LGPD long data retention requirements (up to lifetime for health data) create HNDL risk. Brazil is Latin Americas largest economy and a major financial services market. Banco Central do Brasil participates in BIS quantum readiness initiatives.

label: Denmark CFCS PQC Guidance
description: Danish Centre for Cyber Security post-quantum cryptography guidance for government and critical infrastructure
notes: CFCS (Centre for Cybersikkerhed) published PQC migration guidance for Danish government entities and critical infrastructure operators. Denmark is a Five Eyes+ partner and aligns with EU NIS2 and the EU coordinated PQC roadmap (EU-REC-2024-1101) timelines: national roadmaps by Dec 2026, high-risk migration by Dec 2030, full transition by Dec 2035. CFCS is part of the Danish Defence Intelligence Service.

label: NY DFS 23 NYCRR 500
description: New York Department of Financial Services cybersecurity regulation with explicit encryption and key management requirements
notes: NY DFS 23 NYCRR Part 500 is one of the most prescriptive US financial cybersecurity regulations. Section 500.15 requires encryption of nonpublic information both in transit and at rest using controls identified by the CISO risk assessment. The Second Amendment (effective November 2025) added enhanced requirements for encryption, key management, and incident response. While no explicit PQC mandate, the encryption requirements create a compliance pathway for PQC adoption as NIST standards mature. Applies to all DFS-regulated entities including banks, insurers, and financial service companies operating in New York.

label: ETSI EN 303 645 (IoT Security)
description: ETSI baseline cybersecurity standard for consumer IoT products with cryptographic requirements affecting long-lived devices
deadline: Ongoing (mandatory under EU RED delegated act from August 2025)
notes: ETSI EN 303 645 establishes baseline cybersecurity provisions for consumer IoT products. Provision 5.1 mandates that all cryptography used must follow best practice and be updateable. The EU Radio Equipment Directive (RED) delegated act makes compliance mandatory for wireless IoT devices sold in the EU from August 2025. PQC relevance: IoT devices with 10-15 year lifespans deployed today will operate well into the CRQC era. The crypto-agility requirement (updatable cryptography) supports future PQC migration. Covers smart home, wearables, connected appliances, and industrial IoT.

label: PQCA
description: Post-Quantum Cryptography Alliance — Linux Foundation project advancing PQC adoption through open-source tooling and community collaboration
notes: Founded 2024 by Linux Foundation with AWS, Cisco, IBM, Google, NVIDIA, SandboxAQ, and others. Houses the OQS project and PQ Code Package. Promotes standardized open-source PQC implementations.

label: PQC Coalition
description: PQC Coalition — MITRE-led cooperative advancing quantum-safe migration across critical infrastructure sectors
notes: Launched by MITRE with members from government agencies and industry. Focuses on practical PQC migration guidance, interoperability testing, and sector-specific transition plans.
deprecated_reason: duplicate: PQCC-ROADMAP is the canonical record; pqc-coalition.org redirects to pqcc.org (same organization -- confirmed via canonical tag + matching cached page content), and this row's "MITRE-led" characterization is contradicted by the site's own Founding Members list (MITRE, SandboxAQ, PQShield, IBM Quantum, Microsoft). See id=PQCC-ROADMAP for the canonical (more accurate, better-corroborated) record.

label: QED-C
description: Quantum Economic Development Consortium — NIST-established consortium enabling the quantum ecosystem including PQC readiness assessment
notes: Established by NIST in 2018 under the National Quantum Initiative Act. Over 300 members from industry, academia, and government. Develops use cases, standards alignment, and workforce development for quantum technologies including PQC.

label: APRA CPS 234
description: APRA Prudential Standard CPS 234 Information Security — mandatory for all APRA-regulated entities including banks, insurers, and superannuation funds. Requires robust information security capabilities proportionate to information asset criticality; cryptographic controls are explicitly in scope.
notes: CPS 234 requires information security capabilities commensurate with threats; APRA has flagged quantum computing as an emerging threat in its operational risk guidance. APRA-regulated entities performing cryptographic risk assessments must address PQC transition timelines.

label: ACSC Essential Eight
description: Australian Cyber Security Centre (ACSC) Essential Eight Maturity Model — eight baseline mitigation strategies mandated for Australian government entities and widely adopted in critical infrastructure and finance. Patch management and application hardening strategies directly intersect PQC transition planning.
notes: Essential Eight Maturity Level 3 requires patching within 48 hours for critical vulnerabilities and enforces strong cryptographic controls on internet-facing services. ASD guidance explicitly references PQC readiness as part of cryptographic agility planning under the ISM.

label: Australian Privacy Act (APPs)
description: Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) with Australian Privacy Principles (APPs) — enforced by the Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC). APP 11 requires organisations to take reasonable steps to protect personal information, including cryptographic security controls. Post-quantum transition affects long-term data confidentiality.
notes: The Privacy Act reform (2024) significantly increased penalties for serious or repeated breaches (up to AUM). Harvest-now-decrypt-later attacks on personal data held by financial institutions are directly addressed by PQC transition planning under APP 11.

label: AUSTRAC AML/CTF Act
description: Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act 2006 — enforced by AUSTRAC. Regulated reporting entities (banks, fintechs, crypto exchanges) must maintain secure cryptographic systems for transaction reporting and record-keeping. AML/CTF Rules require integrity and authenticity controls over financial intelligence data.
notes: AUSTRAC AML/CTF Act Chapter 2 requires reporting entities to maintain appropriate authentication and encryption for AUSTRAC reporting channels. The 2024 reforms extending regulated sectors (lawyers, accountants, real estate) increase the number of entities needing cryptographic compliance.

label: OSFI Guideline B-13 — Operational Risk and Resilience (Crypto Controls)
description: Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions guideline B-13 on operational risk and resilience. Covers cryptographic controls for federally regulated financial institutions (FRFIs). Institutions must maintain crypto inventories, assess quantum risk, and implement crypto-agility.
notes: OSFI B-13 (effective Jan 2024) requires FRFIs to manage cryptographic risk under operational resilience. OSFI has signaled alignment with NIST PQC timelines. Financial institutions should expect PQC requirements in forthcoming supervisory guidance. Canada's primary banking regulator (covers banks, insurance, trust companies).

label: Canada CFDIR Quantum-Readiness Best Practices
description: Canadian quantum-readiness best practices and guidelines published by the Centre for Financial Democracy and Innovation Regulation (CFDIR) in partnership with Innovation Science and Economic Development Canada. Covers quantum threat assessment, migration prioritization, and hybrid PQC deployment for financial sector.
notes: CFDIR guidance provides Canada-specific quantum-readiness framework for financial institutions and critical infrastructure. Aligned with NIST PQC standards and CCCS guidance. Covers threat landscape, migration roadmap, algorithm selection, and vendor assessment criteria for Canadian context.
enforcement_body: CFDIR / Innovation Science and Economic Development Canada
vetting_body: Innovation Science and Economic Development Canada

label: UK DSIT CNI PQC Transition Perspectives
description: UK Department for Science, Innovation and Technology perspectives on PQC transition planning from Critical National Infrastructure sectors. Sets expectations for CNI operators (energy, water, transport, finance) to engage with NCSC migration timelines and report readiness.
notes: DSIT published perspectives document (July 2025) requesting CNI sectors develop PQC transition plans aligned with NCSC three-phase roadmap. Represents government expectation — not yet statutory mandate — for critical sectors. Supplements UK-NCSC guidance with sector-specific engagement requirements.
vetting_body: UK Department for Science, Innovation and Technology

label: ACPR (French Banking & Insurance Regulator)
description: Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution — French prudential regulator for banking and insurance sectors, supervised by Banque de France
notes: ACPR supervises French banks and insurers for operational and cyber resilience. DORA compliance (effective Jan 2025) now governs digital operational resilience for regulated entities. ACPR aligns with ANSSI guidance on cryptographic migration. No standalone PQC mandate issued; institutions expected to follow ANSSI recommendations and DORA ICT risk requirements. ACPR participated in European Banking Authority (EBA) guidance on ICT risk management.
library_refs: ANSSI PQC Position Paper;ANSSI PQC Follow-up Paper;ANSSI-PG-083-v3-2026

label: AMF (French Securities Regulator)
description: Autorité des marchés financiers — French securities and financial markets regulator
notes: AMF regulates French financial markets including investment firms, fund managers, and market infrastructure. Subject to DORA (effective Jan 2025) for ICT risk and operational resilience. MiCA introduces crypto-asset market regulation with cybersecurity requirements. No standalone PQC mandate issued; firms expected to follow ANSSI guidance and DORA ICT risk framework for cryptographic agility.
library_refs: ANSSI PQC Position Paper;ANSSI PQC Follow-up Paper

label: DSPF (Defence)
description: Australian Defence Security Principles Framework — cryptography transition requirements for all ADF personnel and cleared contractors
notes: The Defence Security Principles Framework (DSPF) applies to all Australian Defence Organisation personnel, contractors, and cleared entities. PQC transition is governed by ISM-1917 requirements cascading through DSPF. All ADF systems handling PROTECTED and above classifications must achieve ML-DSA-87 / ML-KEM-1024 compliance by end of 2030. Entities holding Defence security clearances must demonstrate a PQC transition plan by end of 2026 per ISM guidance.

label: POPIA
description: South Africa Protection of Personal Information Act — data protection regulation with strong encryption and breach-notification requirements relevant to PQC migration for long-retention data
notes: POPIA Section 19 requires "appropriate, reasonable technical and organisational measures" including encryption for personal information. Long data-retention obligations expose regulated entities to HNDL risk; migration guidance expected from the Information Regulator as NIST PQC suite gains regional traction via SABS.
deprecated_reason: restored from archive 2026-05-03

label: NDPR / NDPA 2023
description: Nigeria Data Protection Regulation + Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 — jointly enforced by the Nigeria Data Protection Commission (NDPC), with explicit encryption obligations for personal data
notes: NDPA 2023 establishes the NDPC and codifies the prior NDPR. Section 39 mandates appropriate technical measures including encryption. NITDA has signalled alignment with NIST PQC suite for regulated sectors (banking, telecoms). No explicit PQC deadline but HNDL exposure on financial and health data is material.
deprecated_reason: restored from archive 2026-05-03

label: Kenya Data Protection Act 2019
description: Kenya Data Protection Act — enforced by the Office of the Data Protection Commissioner (ODPC); imposes encryption-at-rest and in-transit obligations on data controllers
notes: ODPC Guidance Note on Data Protection by Design (2022) requires state-of-the-art cryptography. The Communications Authority of Kenya is coordinating with ODPC on PQC readiness for the telecoms sector. M-Pesa and other mobile-money rails are high-HNDL-exposure systems.
deprecated_reason: restored from archive 2026-05-03

label: Egypt Personal Data Protection Law
description: Egypt Law No. 151 of 2020 on the Protection of Personal Data — enforced by the Egyptian Data Protection Center (DPC); mandates encryption and security controls for personal data processing
notes: Law 151/2020 came into force in October 2020; executive regulations issued 2024. Article 6 requires controllers to implement encryption proportionate to risk. Egypt Financial Regulatory Authority is tracking NIST PQC adoption; no explicit PQC deadline yet but HNDL risk is material for long-lived government records.
deprecated_reason: restored from archive 2026-05-03

label: African Union Malabo Convention
description: African Union Convention on Cyber Security and Personal Data Protection — pan-continental instrument harmonising cybersecurity and data-protection regimes across AU member states
notes: The Malabo Convention entered into force on 8 June 2023 after Mauritania deposited the 15th instrument of ratification. Article 25 requires member states to adopt appropriate technical measures including encryption. The AU Cybersecurity Expert Group 2025 report highlights quantum-safe transition as a priority for regional harmonisation.

label: EUCC v2.0
description: EU Cybersecurity Certification Scheme Agreed Cryptographic Mechanisms v2.0
notes: EUCC Agreed Cryptographic Mechanisms v2.0 now includes PQC algorithms for EU cybersecurity certification. ENISA migrated certification pages to certification.enisa.europa.eu in 2025; old enisa.europa.eu/topics/certification/* URLs now 404.

label: BSI Post-Quantum Standardization Advisory
description: BSI ongoing PQC pre-standardization activity covering algorithm selection commentary, harmonization with NIST FIPS 203/204/205/206, and German-context migration recommendations. Advisory / forward-looking; tracks closely with NIST PQC programme on its own timeline.
notes: Pre-standardization advisory — complements BSI TR-02102 (Algorithmenkatalog) which is the binding cryptographic recommendation.
enforcement_body: BSI (Bundesamt für Sicherheit in der Informationstechnik)

label: PRA Operational Resilience (SS1/21 + cyber)
description: UK PRA supervisory statement on operational resilience, scoped to Tier 1/2 banks, insurers, and major investment firms. The most specific UK supervisory channel on quantum-risk timelines for financial firms.
deadline: Ongoing (FCA cyber guidance is referenced via PRA-supervised firms'' operational-resilience obligations)
notes: Anchor PRA supervisory statement (SS1/21 + 2024 cyber resilience update). FCA cybersecurity guidance for non-PRA-supervised firms is treated as a complementary overlay — not a separate compliance row.
enforcement_body: Bank of England — Prudential Regulation Authority

label: UK ICO Encryption Guidance (UK GDPR Art. 32)
description: UK Information Commissioner''s Office guidance on encryption as a Reasonable Step under UK GDPR Article 32. Codifies current data-at-rest and data-in-transit cryptographic-adequacy expectations; does not mandate PQC.
notes: PQC migration not addressed by ICO directly; UK GDPR Art. 32 reads cryptographic adequacy through industry standards (NIST / NCSC etc.). PQC adoption inherited as those references update.

label: NSM Grunnprinsipper for IKT-sikkerhet (Norway)
description: Norwegian National Security Authority's foundational ICT-security principles — closest Nordic analogue to NIST CSF. NSM publishes explicit PQC positioning and is the unambiguous primary Nordic crypto-guidance authority.
deadline: Ongoing (latest revision tracks NIST PQC standardisation cadence)
notes: Strongest Nordic row — NSM has published explicit PQC positioning beyond the generic NIST cross-reference common to other Nordic agencies.

label: MSB Sweden Cyber Resilience Metodstöd
description: Swedish Civil Contingencies Agency cyber-resilience guidance. MSB is the civil-contingency umbrella; for algorithm-level guidance, cross-reference MSB Metodstöd documents and NCSC-SE bulletins (which sit across SÄPO/MSB depending on topic).
notes: NCSC-SE crypto-specific guidance is the operational layer beneath MSB; PQC migration tracked via Metodstöd updates.

label: NCSC-FI / Traficom Finland Cyber Security Centre Bulletins
description: Finnish National Cyber Security Centre (under Traficom). 'Kyberturvallisuuden tilannekuva' situational picture and technical bulletins drive PQC awareness and timing across Finnish public and critical-infrastructure sectors.
notes: Often underrated regionally; bulletins are technically precise. PQC migration cadence tracks NIST + ENISA alignment.
related_standards: NIST; CRYSTALS-Kyber-Spec-v302; CRYSTALS-Dilithium-Spec-v31; Falcon-Spec-v12; SPHINCS-Plus-Spec-v31; CISA-Quantum-Readiness-Roadmap; NL-PQC-Migration-Handbook-2024

label: Chile ANCI Cybersecurity Standards (Ley 21.663)
description: Chile Agencia Nacional de Ciberseguridad (established by Ley 21.663 / 2023) is the designated national cybersecurity authority. Has already issued binding technical standards across critical-information sectors.
notes: Strongest LATAM cyber-regulator authority today — Tier 1 add per geographic-depth vetting.

label: CNBV Circular Única de Bancos (Mexico)
description: Mexican National Banking and Securities Commission cryptographic-control expectations for banks under the Circular Única de Bancos (CUB). Mature financial-sector cyber-regulation channel — preferred over fragmented NOM cyber standards.
notes: Scoped to Mexican FS regulated entities. Other Mexican cyber bodies (CEDN federal, CNS NOM standards) are out of FS scope and not yet sufficiently consolidated to warrant separate rows.
enforcement_body: Comisión Nacional Bancaria y de Valores (CNBV)

label: Argentina ONTI Cyber Baseline (Secretaría de Innovación Pública)
description: Argentina Oficina Nacional de Tecnologías de Información — the correct cyber authority for federal government (AFIP is the tax authority; BCRA covers financial sector — both are separate from ONTI).
notes: AFIP previously suggested in audit gap was wrong — AFIP is a tax authority, not a cyber regulator. ONTI is the correct government-cyber row; BCRA Comunicación A-series belongs in FS scope.
deprecated_reason: Notes contain no PQC/crypto content (an internal correction about which Argentine agency is the right cyber-regulator reference) — not PQC-related.

label: BACEN Resolution 4.893 (Brazil FS Cyber)
description: Brazilian central bank Resolution 4.893 sets encryption requirements for financial sector institutions. Pairs with ANPD (LGPD) on data-protection cryptographic adequacy; both are well-documented and more mature than most LATAM cyber-regulator entries.
notes: Companion FS row to BRAZIL-ANPD-PQC (data-protection scope). PQC migration will land via the cryptographic-adequacy clause of Resolution 4.893 as NIST + central-bank guidance converge.

label: Indonesia Personal Data Protection Law (UU PDP)
description: Indonesia Law No. 27 of 2022 on Personal Data Protection — establishes a national data-protection regime with explicit obligations on technical and organisational security measures including encryption.
notes: UU PDP entered into force October 2022 with a two-year transition (effective enforcement October 2024). Article 35 requires controllers to implement technical safeguards including encryption proportionate to risk. BSSN (Badan Siber dan Sandi Negara) issues sectoral cryptographic guidance and has begun tracking NIST PQC selections for government systems. No explicit PQC deadline yet but HNDL exposure on long-lived government and banking records is material.
related_standards: Indonesia Law No. 27 of 2022 on Personal Data Protection

label: Thailand Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA 2019)
description: Thailand PDPA B.E. 2562 (2019) — comprehensive data-protection law enforced by the PDPC; requires appropriate security measures for personal data including encryption.
notes: PDPA fully effective June 2022 after deferrals. Section 37 obliges data controllers to provide adequate security measures, with PDPC guidance pointing at internationally recognised standards (ISO 27001, NIST SP 800-series). NCSA (National Cyber Security Agency) issued a 2024 cyber resilience plan that flags post-quantum readiness for critical infrastructure (CII) sectors. ETDA is exploring PQC for the national digital signature framework.

label: Vietnam Cybersecurity Law + Decree 13/2023
description: Vietnam Law on Cybersecurity (2018) plus Decree 13/2023 on Personal Data Protection — joint framework enforced by MIC and the Ministry of Public Security (A05); mandates encryption for personal data processing and cross-border transfers.
notes: Decree 13/2023/NĐ-CP took effect July 2023 and is the operative PDP instrument. Article 26 requires controllers to apply technical security measures including encryption. MIC and A05 publish cryptographic requirements for licensed services; no explicit PQC mandate yet but the Vietnam Government Cipher Commission has tracked NIST FIPS 203/204/205 selections.

label: Philippines Data Privacy Act (RA 10173)
description: Philippines Data Privacy Act of 2012 (Republic Act No. 10173) — enforced by the National Privacy Commission (NPC); mandates encryption for sensitive personal information at rest and in transit.
notes: NPC Circular 16-01 requires AES-256 (or equivalent) for sensitive personal information held by government and material covered entities. DICT (Department of Information and Communications Technology) is the lead on national cybersecurity and tracks NIST PQC outputs for inclusion in the National Cybersecurity Plan 2023-2028. HNDL exposure on national-ID (PhilSys) and banking data is the primary near-term concern.

label: Estonia Cybersecurity Act + RIA PQC Guidance
description: Estonian Cybersecurity Act (2018, updated for NIS2 transposition 2024) — enforced by RIA (Information System Authority); applies to operators of essential and important services; aligns with EUCC and ENISA PQC guidance.
notes: Estonia operates the most mature national digital-signature ecosystem in the EU (ID-card, Mobile-ID, Smart-ID — all eIDAS qualified). RIA has issued written guidance to qualified trust service providers (QTSPs) to begin PQC readiness assessments aligned with ENISA and ETSI TS 119 312. Estonia transposed NIS2 in 2024 with explicit reference to post-quantum migration as a "state of the art" obligation. No fixed PQC deadline but RIA expects QTSPs to publish PQC roadmaps by 2027.

label: Ireland NCSC PQC Guidance + NIS2 Transposition
description: Irish National Cyber Security Centre PQC guidance plus NIS2 transposition via the National Cyber Security Bill 2024 — enforced by NCSC-IE under DECC; aligns with ENISA PQC guidelines and EUCC.
notes: NCSC-IE published the 2023 "Quantum Threat to Cryptography" advisory recommending that public-sector and CII operators begin crypto inventory and PQC readiness work. Ireland transposed NIS2 via the National Cyber Security Bill 2024 (assented 2025) with a "state of the art" cryptography duty that explicitly contemplates PQC migration. NCSC-IE coordinates with ENISA, NCSC-UK, and BSI on cross-border guidance.

label: Belgium NIS2 Transposition + CCB Cybersecurity Strategy
description: Belgian NIS2 transposition (Law of 26 April 2024) + the Centre for Cybersecurity Belgium (CCB) Cybersecurity Strategy 2.0 — covers essential and important entities with explicit reference to post-quantum migration.
notes: Belgium transposed NIS2 via the Law of 26 April 2024 (effective 18 October 2024) with the CCB as competent authority. The CCB Cybersecurity Strategy 2.0 (2021-2025) names post-quantum cryptography as a strategic axis; the CCB has published organisational guidance for crypto-agility inventories. Belgium also hosts the EU institutions which themselves run PQC pilots under the Commission DG DIGIT.

label: Austria NIS2 Transposition + A-SIT Guidance
description: Austrian NIS2 transposition (NISG 2024) + A-SIT (Zentrum für sichere Informationstechnologie - Austria) guidance — covers operators of essential and important services; A-SIT is the recognised national crypto-evaluation body.
notes: Austria transposed NIS2 via NISG 2024 with the Bundesministerium für Inneres (BMI) as competent authority and BKA as policy lead. A-SIT (jointly funded by BMF, BKA, and TU Graz) provides crypto-evaluation services for the national A-Trust QTSP and the Bürgerkarte ecosystem; A-SIT tracks ETSI/BSI PQC guidance and supports A-Trust PQC readiness planning. No fixed PQC deadline; ENISA / ETSI alignment is the operative reference.

label: Poland Cyber Security Act + NASK PQC Program
description: Polish National Cybersecurity System Act (2018, NIS2 amendment 2024) — enforced by Ministry of Digital Affairs with NASK as the national CERT/research body; tracks NIST PQC for public-sector adoption.
notes: Poland transposed NIS2 via a 2024 amendment to the Cybersecurity Act (Ustawa o krajowym systemie cyberbezpieczeństwa). CSIRT NASK and CSIRT GOV publish technical guidance for public-sector cryptography; NASK research division participates in EU PQC projects (PQ-REACT, EuroQCI) and the national Quantum Communications Infrastructure (PIONIER-Q) pilot. No explicit PQC deadline but public-sector procurement is expected to require crypto-agility from 2027.

label: Colombia Habeas Data Law 1581/2012
description: Colombia Statutory Law 1581 of 2012 (Habeas Data) plus Decree 1377/2013 — enforced by SIC (Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio); requires adequate technical measures for personal-data security.
notes: SIC has issued external Circulares on accountability and security (including Circular 003 of 2018) that reference internationally recognised cryptography. MinTIC and ColCERT track NIST PQC outputs; the 2023 National Digital Security Policy (CONPES 3995) flags post-quantum readiness as a forward-looking priority for critical infrastructure and the digital-trust framework.

label: Peru Personal Data Protection Law (Law 29733)
description: Peru Law No. 29733 on Personal Data Protection (2011) + Supreme Decree 003-2013-JUS — enforced by ANPD; requires technical security measures including encryption for sensitive personal data.
notes: ANPD (Autoridad Nacional de Protección de Datos Personales) operates under the Ministerio de Justicia and publishes security guidance referencing ISO 27001 and NIST SP 800-53 control families. PCM-SeGDi (Secretaría de Gobierno y Transformación Digital) leads national digital-trust strategy and tracks NIST PQC outputs through the Peru-OECD Going Digital review. No explicit PQC deadline.

label: Uruguay Personal Data Protection Law (Law 18.331)
description: Uruguay Law 18.331 on Protection of Personal Data + URCDP guidance — enforced by the Personal Data Regulation and Control Unit (URCDP) within AGESIC; Uruguay holds an EU adequacy decision since 2012.
